newsitem.title: USA: Thomas Group sees Q4 loss.
newsitem.headline: Thomas Group sees Q4 loss.

text.p: Thomas Group Inc said Friday that it will record a loss during the fourth quarter of 1996.
While full year 1996 revenues are expected to exceed those of 1995, revenues for the fourth quarter of 1996 are expected to be about $4 million below the $19 million realized in the previous year.
The company had previously predicted a profit in the fourth quarter of 1996, but is currently projecting a loss of $0.35 to $0.40 per share.

This expected loss compares to a profit of $0.33 per share in the fourth quarter of 1995. The shortfall is based on several major factors including; delays in program starts, the costs of personnel adjustments, and losses at Interlink due to spending on product improvements.
The company attributed the results to significant delays in anticipated business closings around the world, causing decreased revenues in the fourth quarter of 1996.
It also pointed to increased marketing spending. It said traditionally, referencability and word of mouth advertising had been adequate to provide for planned revenue growth.

Management increased spending in 1996 on marketing and visibility programs and to establish specific industry business units. These investments included the opening of a Singapore office for future growth in the Asia/Pacific region, and the addition of industry specific resources in business units such as Automotive and Aviation.
These investments should provide renewed growth in 1997. The related expenses, however, will reduce our short term profitability."

Philip Thomas, CEO, said in a statement, "While contract delays in all regions hurt 1996 performance, sales in the United States are expected to be up significantly versus 1995. We are disappointed with our European results and have revamped our New Business Acquisition process based on our success in the U.S. This has resulted in a doubling of qualified leads entering the first quarter of 1997."
